correctness.rationale: For all integers d>=3 and -1<a<1 the exact identities t-u=a, ut=d(1-a^2)/(d+1)^2, v^2=u^2+dut and 1-||point(s)||^2=dut(s-1/d)^2 imply containment. The d+1 explicit normalized contact points form a regular simplex with equal positive weights d/(d+1), whose first moment is zero and second moment is I_d; the sufficient direction of John's theorem proves unique global optimality. Exact slicing and dominated convergence give the hemisphere/thin-cap volume ratios; elementary expansions give all three dimension regimes. Standalone supplementary checks ran successfully; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The maximal ellipsoid of a one-cut Euclidean ball is a canonical affine rounding problem; this result classifies every genuinely truncated cap in all dimensions d>=3 and gives a cut-independent optimal regular-simplex contact configuration. Exact volume-ratio benchmarks and a nontrivial \(d^{-1}\) versus \(d^{-1/2}\) axial-scale crossover make the family an informative geometric and high-dimensional benchmark, not a mere isolated numerical special case.
